title: Sum of Beauty in the Array
notes:
## Intuition

Checking "greater than everything to the left and smaller than everything to the right" for each index by scanning both sides costs O(n²). But "greater than everything to the left" only needs the **maximum** of the left part, and "smaller than everything to the right" only needs the **minimum** of the right part. A running prefix maximum and a precomputed suffix minimum answer both in O(1). The score-1 test only looks at the two neighbours.

## Approach

1. Build `suffixMin` from right to left: `suffixMin[i]` is the smallest value in `nums[i..n-1]`.
2. Keep `prefixMax`, the largest value in `nums[0..i-1]`, starting with `nums[0]`.
3. For each interior `i`: if `prefixMax < nums[i] < suffixMin[i + 1]`, add 2; otherwise, if `nums[i - 1] < nums[i] < nums[i + 1]`, add 1.
4. Fold `nums[i]` into `prefixMax` before moving on, and return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 3]`. From the right, `suffixMin = [1, 2, 3]`. Start with `prefixMax = 1`. The only interior index is `i = 1`: `1 < 2` and `2 < suffixMin[2] = 3`, so it scores 2 and `total = 2`, the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass to fill `suffixMin`, one pass to score.
- Space: O(n) for `suffixMin`.

## Pitfalls

- The comparisons are strict: an equal value to the left or right breaks the score-2 rule (`[1, 2, 2, 3, 4]`).
- Score 2 replaces score 1; an index never earns both, so use `else if`.
- Compare with `suffixMin[i + 1]`, not `suffixMin[i]`, which includes `nums[i]` itself and would never be larger.
- Update `prefixMax` after scoring `i`, so it only covers the elements left of `i`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `suffixMin[i]` | smallest value from index `i` to the end |
| `prefixMax` | largest value strictly left of the current `i` |
| `total` | sum of the scores so far |
| `i` | the interior index being scored |

narration.3: suffixMin[i] will hold the smallest value from index i to the end of the array.
narration.4: The suffix that starts at the last index holds just that value.
narration.5: Fill the rest from right to left...
narration.6: ...each entry is the smaller of this value and the minimum after it.
narration.9: prefixMax is the largest value left of the current index; before index 1 that is nums[0].
narration.11: Score each interior index; the first and last are skipped.
narration.12: Above everything on the left and below everything on the right?
narration.14: Otherwise, is it strictly between its two neighbours?
narration.17: Include nums[i] in the prefix maximum before moving to the next index.
